newsitem.title: USA: Apple CEO suspends executive bonuses.
newsitem.headline: Apple CEO suspends executive bonuses.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Gilbert Amelio told the company's annual meeting he was suspending Apple's executive bonus plan until the company returned to profitability.

"Let me assure you that my highest priority is to get this company in the black as early as possible," Amelio told Apple shareholders. Amelio said that when he took over at the helm of the troubled computer company one year ago, it faced five crises, which he has sought to address. "We were broke," he said, adding that financial liquidity was so tight the company barely had enough reserves to manage its daily business.
Amelio's comments came one day after the company announced another restructuring and less than a month after Apple stunned Wall Street with a $120 million loss in the first quarter of fiscal 1997.
Amelio, who was interrupted several times by shareholders, did not provide specifics about the restructuring, or how many jobs might be cut as Apple seeks to reduce its costs.

However, he said the company planned to suspend its executive bonus plan until Apple returned to profitability. Recently, Apple officials said they expect to return to the black by the end of the 1997 fiscal year in September.
The decision to suspend the bonus program comes after the company revealed some executives received substantial bonuses last year when Apple reported an unexpected fourth quarter profit.
The payout was the result of a change in the compensation plan which allowed the executives to receive bonuses based on the company's fourth quarter results rather than the full year's.
For the fourth quarter, which ended in September, Apple reported a profit of $25 million, surprising Wall Street, which had been expecting Apple to report a modest loss.

Much of that profit, however, came from a one-time gain Apple recognized for an inventory adjustment. Without that gain, Apple would have reported a modest loss or would have simply broken even, one analyst estimated.

Based on that one profitable quarter, Apple's senior executives received "175 percent of their special bonus target," according to Apple's proxy statement. Amelio, who had a separate compensation agreement with the company, received a $648,000 bonus on top of his $990,000 base salary. Apple did not disclose the bonuses of the other executives.
Apple officials said the special bonus plan was meant to encourage executives to meet their turnaround goals.
"It was basically to motivate them to achieve profitability," said Apple spokeswoman Nancy Paxton. She said the executives had expected financial performance to improve following the fourth quarter.

In addition to the immediate liquidity crisis Amelio said he faced on taking the helm last year, he said the company faced a quality crisis, a crisis in its corporate culture, a crisis over development of its next-generation operating system and an underlying fragmentation underlying it all.

"The company was simply doing too much, moving in too many directions and not enough of it was profitable," Amelio said. "I sometimes think that, when it comes to cool new projects, Apple's eyes were bigger than its stomach."
Businesses were so fragmented that he said the company was using no fewer than seven different financial systems and its forecasting system was "completely inadequate".

Amelio outlined actions he has taken to address these crises, including the decision in December to acquire NeXT Software for $400 million to help Apple develop a stable, high-performance new operating system.

After the annual meeting, which was held near Apple's headquarters, Amelio told reporters the suspension of executive bonuses would remain in effect until the board deems Apple to have returned to sustainable profits.

Amelio said it would relate to merit-based cash and stock grant bonuses, but not to stock option plans, many of which he noted have already been agreed on an individual basis. --sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau +1 415 846 5400
